source.author: verg
source.text: Atque hic Priamiden laniatum corpore toto Deiphobum videt et lacerum crudeliter ora, ora manusque ambas, populataque tempora raptis auribus, et truncas inhonesto volnere nares.
source.text_original: Atque hic Priamiden laniatum corpore toto / Deiphobum videt et lacerum crudeliter ora, / ora manusque ambas, populataque tempora raptis / auribus, et truncas inhonesto volnere nares.
source.text_english: And here he sees Deiphobus, son of Priam, with his whole body mangled, his face brutally torn, both face and hands ravaged, his temples stripped by the torn-off ears, and his nostrils cut off in an ugly wound.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: describam nunc ego diuersas hominum calamitates, truncas nares, effossos oculos, semiustos pedes, luridas manus, tumentes aluos, exile femur, crura turgentia et de exesis ae putridis carnibus uermiculos bullientes?
reuse.text_original: describam nunc ego diuersas hominum calamitates, truncas nares, effossos oculos, semiustos pedes, luridas manus, tumentes aluos, exile femur, crura turgentia et de exesis ae putridis carnibus uermiculos bullientes?
reuse.text_english: Shall I now describe the various misfortunes of men: noses cut off, eyes gouged out, feet half-burned, livid hands, swollen bellies, a shrunken thigh, legs swollen, and little worms seething out of their eaten-away and rotten flesh?
